title: Stripe Nears $10 Billion Deal to Acquire AI Model Marketplace OpenRouter
excerpt: The payments giant is in advanced talks to buy the startup that routes developer requests across 400+ AI models, marking an aggressive push into AI infrastructure.
body:
• Stripe is in talks to acquire OpenRouter for roughly $10 billion, according to The Wall Street Journal, representing an eightfold jump from its $1.3 billion valuation in May.
  • OpenRouter gives developers access to over 400 large language models from providers like OpenAI, Anthropic, and open-source alternatives through a single API.
  • The deal comes as Stripe simultaneously pursues a $53 billion bid for PayPal, signaling a sweeping expansion beyond payments.
  • Founded in 2023 by Alex Atallah, OpenRouter processes hundreds of trillions of tokens monthly and serves over 5 million developers.

Stripe, the $159 billion payments giant, is in advanced talks to acquire OpenRouter, a fast-growing startup that helps developers route requests across hundreds of artificial intelligence models, in a deal that could value the company at roughly $10 billion.

The Wall Street Journal first reported the talks on July 23, citing people familiar with the matter. A transaction could be announced soon, though discussions remain fluid and could still collapse or attract a rival bidder. Several other large technology companies had also been weighing deals for OpenRouter before Stripe emerged as the leading suitor.

From $1.3 Billion to $10 Billion in Months

The reported price tag represents a dramatic markup. OpenRouter closed a $113 million Series B round in May at a $1.3 billion valuation, led by CapitalG, Alphabet's growth-venture fund. Other investors included NVentures (Nvidia's venture arm), ServiceNow Ventures, MongoDB Ventures, Snowflake Ventures, Databricks Ventures, and existing backers Andreessen Horowitz and Menlo Ventures.

https://x.com/Techmeme/status/2089082490199916729

A sale at approximately $10 billion would value the company at nearly eight times its price from just two months prior — a jump that underscores how central the platform has become to how businesses deploy AI.

What OpenRouter Does

Founded in 2023 by Alex Atallah, who previously co-founded NFT marketplace OpenSea, OpenRouter operates as an aggregation platform that gives developers access to over 400 large language models through a single API. Users can compare performance, switch providers on the fly, and optimize for cost or capability without building separate integrations for each model provider.

The platform routes requests across closed-source models from OpenAI and Anthropic as well as open-source alternatives like DeepSeek. It now handles traffic for millions of users and processes hundreds of trillions of tokens each month. The company charges a percentage fee on top of each model's underlying cost — a structure remarkably similar to how payments processors operate.

"Stripe handles payment complexity in an elegant way so we can focus on making AI models accessible and high-quality for developers everywhere."

— Alex Atallah, CEO, OpenRouter

Strategic Logic for Stripe

The acquisition would mark a significant step outside payments for Stripe, which processes transactions for much of the internet. The two companies already have a deep partnership: OpenRouter uses Stripe for billing, tax handling, fraud protection, and global payments. Stripe's integration lets developers route model requests through OpenRouter while Stripe automatically tracks usage, applies dynamic pricing, and manages invoicing.

Acquiring OpenRouter would let Stripe own the metering and billing infrastructure for AI inference — effectively controlling the tollbooth on an exploding volume of AI-driven API calls. Many companies now want access to a range of AI models to control spending and reduce dependence on any single provider, making OpenRouter's routing layer increasingly essential.

The deal also follows Stripe's broader expansion into AI infrastructure and stablecoin payments. CEO Patrick Collison described the first quarter of 2026 as the beginning of an AI "singularity" for commerce.

A Busy Dealmaker

The OpenRouter talks come as Stripe simultaneously pursues a far larger target: a bid for PayPal in collaboration with Advent International that would value the payments company at roughly $53 billion. Between the two deals, Stripe is signaling an intent to transform from a pure-play payments processor into a broader technology infrastructure company.

What's Next

A deal could be announced in the near term, but talks could still fall through or attract competing offers. If completed, the acquisition would be one of the largest in the AI infrastructure space and would reshape how developers access and pay for AI model usage. For the fast-growing ecosystem of companies building on top of multiple AI models, Stripe's ownership of the routing layer would concentrate significant market power in a single player.
nri_angle: Indian-origin tech founders and developers are heavily represented in the AI infrastructure ecosystem that OpenRouter serves, and the deal's outcome could affect how thousands of Indian-American-led startups access and pay for AI models.
